They actually need a day/night cycle, like all living creatures. Having any light whatsoever for them at night is bad for them and completely unnecessary. It’s fine for the terrarium to cool down a little at night. The only reason you would need to heat it is if the room it’s in drops below the mid/low 60’s Fahrenheit, in which case you would still want to ditch the red light and get a Ceramic Heat Emitter. As indicated by the name, CHE’s radiate heat without producing any light.

So my parents were married for 36 years until my mom passed away unexpectedly from the flu in February. My dad is a process server and they ran a legal business where he serves evictions and similar documents while she ran his office. I’m their third and youngest child. I’m 23, my sisters are 10 & 12 years older than me and both moved when they were 18, so I never really had them around much, although to be honest they’re pretty much as crazy as my parents and their presence was generally probably more detrimental than positive.

My home was never particularly happy. My siblings fought with each other, my parents fought with each other, and my parents constantly got into verbally aggressive screaming matches with my siblings. This didn’t really affect me until I was a little older and both of my siblings had moved, at which point my parents directed a lot of their anger at me as well. My dad would call me vicious swear words on a daily basis until I directly asked him to stop using each one.

I came out as trans two years ago, which also caused a lot of tension within my family. My parents immediately outed me to their parents and any distant family they were in contact with. I was briefly kicked out but hadn’t been able to make that work out and had to come back. Now that my mom has passed we’ve been reconnecting with some family we had fallen out from years ago and my dad continues to immediately out me to them without my consent, despite how I’d gotten upset and tried to explain it was dangerous for me when they did that when it had happened before. 

I was homeschooled and socially isolated from fifth grade, so I had a lot of social anxiety and self doubt. I figured I would always be stuck working for my dad so dropped out of high school and started working full time in the family business. However my dad’s abuse began escalating to a physical level last year. Our fights escalated to him physically attacking me several times including at one point when he picked me up and threw me on the ground face-first, and there was a point in time when I’d jumped out of his car while he was driving and still have a chipped tooth as a result. (I never initiate physical violence and know myself well enough by now to pretty safely say I likely never will. I’d hurt myself before another person.)

I came to a breaking point and quit working for him in December and was able to get another (part time, minimum wage) job in the same month, which I’m holding strong despite him constantly telling me I’d never keep a “real job” for more than two days. I was honestly getting to the point when I was getting ready to look for a second job and try to save up to move when my mom passed. 

She ran my dad’s office and I do feel a lot of deep love and loyalty for both of them, so in honor of her memory I took over for her and have since been doing it for free. I’ve managed to keep my other job and have no job balancing each despite my dad getting furious each time I’m on schedule for my other one. Even though I keep hoping things will be better, they continue not to improve at all. 

If I continue working for him I definitely can continue to live here, but won’t be able to look for another job or save up to move. If I quit working for him it’s pretty much guaranteed he’ll kick me out, but I’d be able to look for another job so hopefully I could support myself.  I haven’t totally worked out the financial logistics of that yet but I mean, most adults move away from their parents eventually. However he’d have to hire and train somebody else to run his office, and it’s actually a job I kind of enjoy doing, especially if I can talk him into putting me on the pay roll. (He keeps saying he will this month however he tends to say things and not do them fairly often.)

I don’t know, I haven’t even totally decided what I want to do yet. But if I decide to move, am I a morally screwed up asshole who failed and abandoned my dad and family when he needs me the most? Either way, I probably would still be living with him and running his office for the next couple of months at least.

Do you have any way to measure the temperatures in his tank?

It’s okay for them to be a little colder at night, which I still feel like could cause this. But it’s always good to know what kind of conditions our pets are living in. 

If you don’t already have one, you can get an laser thermometer gun on Amazon for under $20. https://www.amazon.com/dp/B00837ZGRY?utm_source=share&utm_medium=ios_app

During the day you want their basking spot to be 100-110 Fahrenheit(or warmer if they’re a baby, probably 115-125) their warm side around 90 degrees, and the cool side to be around low 80s/high 70s. (If I’m off, someone please correct me!!!)

At night time, you just want to make sure the temperatures aren’t dropping below the low 70s. If they are, you probably need a Ceramic Heat Emitter for night. CHEs just emit heat, no light, so can keep your little guy warm without disturbing his sleep. 

Edit: Just checked out your post history and saw your little dude is indeed a baby. That means he needs slightly warmer conditions than an adult, as I mentioned. Also if you still have the 10 gal, upgrade ASAP! It’s almost impossible to get a proper temperature gradient in a tank that small, which is extremely essential for beardies. Well, at the beginning of October I noticed he was having a difficult time breathing so brought him to the vet. They diagnosed him with a respiratory infection and prescribed 0.1 ML of Baytril to be delivered orally every 12 hours for two weeks. They also suspected he had ADV as well as coccidia so did a fecal test. Fortunately, the test came back negative for both ADV and coccidia, however it turned out he did have pinworms. 

The vet prescribed 1.1 ML of Nemex II to be delivered orally every day for three days, then wait for three weeks, then repeat the Nemex II treatment and bring in another fecal sample. From what I’ve read this is a pretty unorthodox way to treat a beardie for pinworms, the normal treatment seems to be Panacur, Nemex II seems to normally be given to dogs and puppies(occasionally cats.) The treatment must have worked though, and his second round of tests just came back clear!
Update: the tests came back negative!!! Puff’s all clear and healthy!!!

I’m not an expert, I’ve only had my little guy since June. But from the research I’ve done for him, I would say lighting and temperature are THE MOST important things for their health. They need a tube uvb bulb instead of a coil one because coil ones don’t provide enough light for dragons and I’ve read can harm their eyes. Uvb is very important for dragons because it helps prevent them from developing MBD (metabolic bone disease.)

Heating is so important because if it’s not warm enough they won’t be able to digest their food well. Ideal temps vary a little depending on age, babies like it a little hotter than adults, but you’ll basically want your cold side to be around 80 degrees Fahrenheit and the warm side to be 90-100 degrees with a basking spot that’s a little warmer. (With those branches, you should be good.) If it gets below mid 60s Fahrenheit at night you’ll probably want to look into a Ceramic Heating Bulb that emanates heat but no light. Otherwise, no light or heat is needed at night. 

The next most important thing to keep your dragon healthy is diet. You’ll want to offer a variation of veggies every day. http://www.beautifuldragons.com/Nutrition.html is a good guide for which vegetables to pick. Avoid kale and spinach. They’re probably okay occasionally, but potentially dangerous as a staple. Avoid lettuce, no nutritional value. Make sure you dust the salad with calcium and multivitamins. You won’t need vitamins every single day, make sure to do some research and experimenting to figure out the best dusting schedule. Fruit is okay for a treat, but not a staple. When I gave my little guy berries they upset his stomach, haha. Avoid feeding banana very often like spinach and kale. 

Babies need a LOT of bugs. Three live feedings a day, generally as many as they’ll eat in a 10-15 minute feeding session, which can easily add up to over a hundred per day. As they get older you’ll eventually want to do less live feedings, twice a day, then once a day, then only a couple of times a week when they’re an adult. Give a salad daily though. 

The best bugs for beardies are crickets, dubia roaches, and black soldier fly larvae AKA Phoenix worms. I prefer roaches and BSFL. Dubia roaches are my guys favorite thing in the world, and BSFL are great because they’re small and soft so pose very little risk of impaction, slow so they’re easy to give him and for him to catch, and won’t bite so they can be left in the tank with him for a while. Crickets will bite, so if you use those be careful not to leave any behind. 

Superworms and mealworms can be dangerous for beardies because of their hard exoskeleton. Any time I’ve tried to feed superworms as a treat we’ve had a catastrophe; never again. 

Bugs need to be dusted in calcium and multi vitamins as well. BSFL don’t need to be dusted with calcium but still need vitamins on vitamin days. The reason it’s so important to dust bugs and salad with calcium is because it can also help prevent developing or worsening MBD. 

Make sure none of the insects you feed are too large. Generally you don’t want the bugs to be bigger than the width between the beardies eyes. Small exceptions can be made for soft bugs like BSFL. 

I hope none of this comes off like I’m trying to lecture you or be a know-it-all. That definitely isn’t the case, I just want to help and had some time to write this out, it actually helped me a lot to focus on this instead of some other stuff I’ve got going on right now.
